top.title: No rest for Michigan basketball as Thanksgiving week brings busy schedule
top.description: The schedule is about to heat up for Michigan basketball. The Wolverines had few days off this week, with a six-day gap on the nonconference slate. But they'll make up for that in a hurry, with Michigan (3-) playing at least four – and potentially five – games in an eight-day stretch to close out November. That begins with a matchup against Villanova (3-2) on Saturday, Nov. 21 (7 p.m., Fox), at Xfinity Mobile Arena, home of the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers . It's a rematch of, among other games, last December's blowout by the Wolverines in Ann Arbor. Much as U-M has, Villanova has turned over its roster in its second season under coach Kevin Willard, with senior Tyler Perkins as the only returning player from last year's meeting. STEP IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION: Michigan basketball finding its identity, forged by foe's speed "It's becoming less and less where there's real continuity in programs year to year," said U-M coach Mike Boynton Jr. With the season still in its opening month, Boynton said he generally likes to focus practices in extended stretches like this past week on self-improvement − working on rotations, installing schemes and identifying solutions to early problems – rather than focusing on scouting reports on opponents. But this week, an illness went through the team in recent days, leaving a number of players were limited or held out as a result. "It's been more individual stuff as opposed to team, which I hate because I would love to have used the time more productively with our whole group," Boynton said. "Just wasn't really an option this time for us." Some of those individual focuses included more reps for Joseph Hartmann, a freshman wing, who returned to the court for the first time in a month Tuesday. Boynton said Thursday's practice would give the team "a little bit better indication" of where his conditioning is, but there's a chance he's available this weekend. U-M also continues to work on Jalen Reed's conditioning. The LSU transfer suffered season-ending leg injuries the past two years and was held out last week against Marquette after he felt a bit of soreness. He's expected to be available this weekend as well. As for the matchup, despite the roster shuffle, the Wildcats have at least one familiar face: Devin Royal – a three-year player at Ohio State and former teammate of Roddy Gayle Jr. – who leads 'Nova at 14.8 points per game and is second at 7.4 rebounds. Perkins also averages 12.4 points per game while Italian freshman center Luigi Suigo, who stands 7 feet 3, is averaging 12 points and 9.3 rebounds. top.title: ‘Can you blame him?’ – NFL fans defend Al Michaels after Texans vs. Colts snoozefest
top.description: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images Al Michaels has come under a lot of scrutiny this season for his commentary on Amazon Prime’s broadcast of Thursday Night Football. At 82 years old, Michaels is working into the very back end of his career in NFL broadcasting, which has clearly led to some underwhelming performances up in the booth. Fans have expressed their disappointment with some of his play-calling on a number of occasions. Thursday night’s game between the Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts once again saw a mellow Michaels in the booth. However, on this occasion, NFL fans jumped to his defense following what was one of the most boring games of the season. NFL fans defend Al Michaels after boring Thursday Night Football game The Colts are now seeing out their season after trading away most of their star players. That was on full display on Thursday evening as the Texans only gave up three points in what was never a real contest in Texas. Despite Michaels’ commentary lacking any enthusiasm, NFL fans were largely accepting, given the lack of spark on the field. ‘If you watched the game, this is the interest level he should have had. It was abysmal !! Horrible game to watch,’ responded one fan on X. ‘Do you blame him?? I lost interest in the game as soon as it started,’ added another. The game ended 26-3 to the Texans, with Amazon’s crew taking aim at Michaels during the game with a dig at the amount of vegetables he consumes. The level of interest surrounding the game on Thursday was clearly at an all-time low. ‘The game deserved that level of emotion…’ another NFL fan replied. ‘Just stop. You want him to get excited over that? Are you insane?’ said another. There have been a number of exciting Thursday Night Football games this season, but this week’s was not one of those. ‘In his defense, he was watching this abysmal game at the time,’ replied one NFL fan. top.title: Drake Allen went from high school manager to Motor City Cruise standout
top.description: For most people, getting cut by your junior varsity basketball team represents the end of their hoops dreams. But for Drake Allen, it was the beginning. The Motor City Cruise guard couldn't imagine life without basketball, so he became the team manager during his sophomore year at Westlake High School in Eagle Mountain, Utah. That meant picking up towels, running the scoreboard, keeping stats, rebounding basketballs during warmups and practice and, if he was lucky, stepping in and playing if they needed an extra guy. "I had a moment that sophomore year where I decided, how much do I love the game? " Allen said. "Am I going to be a manager? And if I was a manager the rest of my life and eventually a coach, that’s what I was gonna be. Just decided to stick around the game as long as I could and it ended up working out." BEST IN THE WEST? How a battered Pistons team solved Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs Thankfully for Allen, he underwent a growth spurt and the rest of his path began to click into place, going from around 5 feet 10 when he was initially cut to 6-4 en route to the Detroit Pistons ' G League affiliate. He played two years at the junior college level before transferring to mid-majors Southern Utah, Utah Valley and then finally two years at Utah State, before joining the Pistons' summer league team this past offseason. Now, he's off to a strong start with the Cruise and proving that there's still more ahead for his basketball journey, which once looked destined for the sideline. "Being able to be a little bit bigger, a little bit more athletic, that all came with time," He said. "But that first year, being able to grow my mind and my love for basketball, it grew even more. When someone takes something away from you, you realize how much it means to you. That’s what happened. Allowed me to become an even better player, I guess." Through five games with the Cruise during the G LEague's Tip-Off Tournament, Allen is averaging a team-high nine assists, along with 16.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 steals. His 45 assists are the most in franchise history through the first five games of the season, and also leads all G League rookies. Beyond passing the ball, Allen plays both end of the floor. During Las Vegas Summer League, his defensive effort and physicality shined. Allen comes from a sports family – his dad, Roque, played soccer in college, while his mom, Tamra, played volleyball. Allen recalls obsessively watching basketball as a young child, and every day after school. His love for the game only deepened as he grew older. "There’s something you can get better at better every day, and there’s not many things that you can continue to get better at over and over and add new things," he said. "You become obsessed with it, and I think that’s where the love comes from." He wasn't recruited in high school, so he began at Snow College in Ephraim, Utah. top.title: How can Ohio State football beat Nebraska in final regular-season road game?
top.description: Here are three keys for No. 14 Ohio State at Nebraska on Nov. 21: Play clean Penalties have plagued Ohio State throughout the season, especially away from Columbus. The Buckeyes have committed multiple false starts in each of their past three road games, including as many as five at Iowa last month. The trend continued at USC , where OSU mixed up cadences, leading to pre-snap issues during freshman quarterback Luke Fahey ’s first start. If they are going to finish above .500 on the road, the Buckeyes must avoid the self-inflicted mistakes that have put them behind the chains. Fahey’s added experience should help reduce communication breakdowns, but the Buckeyes need to be more disciplined across the board in a tough environment. Contain Anthony Colandrea The Buckeyes caught a break last week as Northwestern ’s Aidan Chiles remained sidelined with an injury, sparing them from facing one of the Big Ten’s best dual-threat quarterbacks. They won’t be as fortunate this week with Colandrea behind center for Nebraska. Colandrea leads the conference’s quarterbacks with 447 rushing yards. His legs pose a threat on scrambles as well as designed runs, making it paramount that the Buckeyes contain him in the pocket when plays break down. Colandrea has 22 runs of at least 10 yards, the second-most in the Big Ten behind Indiana running back Turbo Richard. Get off the field on third down Ohio State's struggles getting stops on third down have persisted for weeks, allowing teams to convert more than 40% of the time over the past four games. The defense has proven vulnerable even in third-and-long situations. The Buckeyes ranked 86 th in third-down defense through Week 11. They won’t find much reprieve at Nebraska, as the Cornhuskers can sustain drives. They rank 13 th in the Football Bowl Subdivision with a third-down conversion rate of 47.8%. The Buckeyes fared better against Northwestern, especially late in the game, with more traditional fronts with four down linemen and will look for the momentum to continue. Key matchup Ohio State offensive line vs. Nebraska defensive line It’s no coincidence Fahey put together arguably his best performance against Northwestern. After he was under duress on 32.3% of his dropbacks against Oregon and USC, he faced pressure on just 14.7% of his dropbacks against the Wildcats, according to Pro Football Focus. The protection allowed him to be more efficient and deliver at key junctures of the game. The Cornhuskers present a challenge up front as their 27 sacks are the fourth-most in the Big Ten, and they have posted multiple sacks in all but two games this year, though sack leader Jahsear Whittington will be unavailable. The pass rush puts the spotlight on the Buckeyes’ offensive line and whether they can continue to keep the pocket clean for Fahey after appearing more stable a week earlier. top.title: Top three midfielders in the world? Where Roy Keane-esque Arsenal ace Declan Rice sits in the global pecking order for ex-England star Paul Ince
top.description: Declan Rice Roy Keane - Getty/GOAL Declan Rice has become Roy Keane and Bryan Robson-esque, former England star Paul Ince has told GOAL, with Arsenal’s Premier League title winner considered to be one of the top three midfielders in world football. Ex-Manchester City ace Rodri sits at the top of that talent tree, but an all-action Three Lions talisman has taken up a standing among the global elite. Record-breaking transfer to Arsenal Few could have predicted that would be the case when seeing Rice - who was released by Chelsea as a youngster - step out of the academy ranks at West Ham. No definitive role had been nailed down at that point, with regular game time being seen at centre-half . He eventually settled on a holding role in the middle of the park, with full potential being unlocked in the engine room. Rice captained the Hammers to Conference League glory in 2023. A matter of weeks later, with his stock having been on the rise for some time, a record-breaking £105 million ($138m) transfer to Arsenal was completed - as he became the most expensive British player in history . Game has changed with Gunners Further progression and development has been enjoyed in north London, with the affable 27-year-old now more of a buccaneering No.8 - for club and country - than a water-carrying six that is happy to win the ball and move it quickly on to others. There has been talk of Rice becoming a Ballon d’Or contender , having seen international colleague Harry Kane claim that prize in 2026 , with his value to any given cause clear to see - with a top-flight crown being captured with the Gunners last season. Widely considered to be one of the most complete midfielders in world football, Rice can claim to rub shoulders with the very best in the business - leading to comparisons being drawn with iconic box-to-box performers that once starred for Manchester United and England. One of the best in the business Ince, who filled that role himself for the Red Devils and Three Lions, told GOAL - while speaking in association with freebets.com - when asked if Rice is a top-three midfielder on the planet: “Rodri's the best midfielder in the world. “Jude Bellingham, would we class him as a midfielder? top.title: UConn women's basketball coach Geno Auriemma sounds off on NIL, recruiting
top.description: STORRS — For decades, UConn women’s basketball could walk into almost any gym in America and expect to be in the conversation for the nation’s best players. Now, as name, image and likeness (NIL) reshapes the sport’s power structure, coach Geno Auriemma says the Huskies are navigating a recruiting landscape where their prestige, winning and player development no longer carry the same weight. “We don't have cachet with guys that are getting a million dollars to go play someplace. They're getting the cachet,” Auriemma said after Thursday’s practice. “I just don't see the value of paying a high school kid a million dollars that hasn't dribbled the ball one time in college.” UConn falls in polls: UConn women’s basketball drops four spots in latest USA Today poll UConn by the numbers: Why UConn women's basketball needs more offense behind Sarah Strong Auriemma’s comments came as UConn’s 2027 recruiting class has taken shape in a way that would have been almost unthinkable for much of his tenure. The Huskies landed five-star guard Sydney Savoury, ESPN’s No. 9-ranked prospect, but missed on several of the nation’s top targets. No. 1 recruit Kaleena Smith narrowed her choices to USC, UCLA and Arizona State after UConn was widely viewed as a contender. No. 2 prospect Ivanna Wilson Manyacka committed to UCLA after the Huskies made her Top 5. No. 8 recruit Haylen Ayers chose Vanderbilt, while Hungarian standout Kinga Josepovits picked Duke. UConn was among the finalists for both prospects. UConn’s success has been built on being the destination for the top players in their respective recruiting classes. Whether that be Maya Moore, Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd or Tina Charles, the Huskies usually have no problem finding the best players in the nation to commit to playing in Storrs. But lately, the effects of NIL have been shown. According to 247Sports, UConn hasn’t reeled in a Top 10 recruiting class in the last two seasons. In 2026, the Huskies ranked 27th, and the year before, they were 17th. Auriemma and his staff have still gotten high-end talent, just not at the same volume. Last cycle, UConn signed five-star center Olivia Vukosa — the No. 2 ranked player in the country. But that was the only domestic recruit Auriemma brought into the program as he filled the rest of his roster with international players such as Jovana Popovic and Marine Dursus. As more schools pour resources into women’s basketball, Auriemma believes the shifting landscape is less an indictment of UConn and more of a reflection of the sport’s growth. “There's more schools that are investing more resources and the players are attracted to places that maybe in the past they weren't,” Auriemma said. “I think the growth of the game reflects that.” As the game changes, Auriemma has not altered his recruiting philosophy. top.description: Barcelona monitoring 17-year-old Girona defensive talent amid Premier League interest According to ESPN (h/t SPORT ), Barcelona have added Girona youngster Holmes Junior to their list of potential defensive targets as the club continue to assess their options at centre-back. The Catalans are closely following the 17-year-old’s progress, although they face competition from several Premier League clubs who are also monitoring his development. Strengthening the centre of defence has become a priority at Camp Nou, particularly after injuries have disrupted Hansi Flick’s options this season. While experienced options like Alessandro Bastoni are being considered , Barça continue to keep an eye on young talents with a long-term view, leading to their interest in the likes of Ruud Nijstad and now Holmes Junior. Already a first-team player at 17 Holmes Junior has enjoyed a steady rise to prominence since joining Girona’s academy in the summer of 2025. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Girona FC (@gironafc) The 17-year-old starlet spent time in Real Madrid’s youth system before making the move to Gimnastic in 2024 and subsequently signing for Girona, where he has continued to progress. In fact, such has been his development that Junior has already broken into the Girona first-team squad this season, making ten appearances – nine in La Liga 2 and one in Copa del Rey – with even a goal to his name. The youngster has also made four appearances for the Spain Under-18 national team. This potential and rapid ascent at Girona has put him on the radar of clubs looking to invest in promising young defenders, including Barcelona. Barcelona among clubs keeping an eye Along with the immense promise he has shown, what appeals to Barcelona is that Junior is a left-footed centre-back comfortable with playing out from the back, a profile that the club are eager to add to their ranks. top.title: Kane trading goals for assists as Bayern await scoring surge
top.description: Kane trading goals for assists as Bayern await scoring surge Despite racking up 43 shots and being denied by the woodwork on three separate occasions, Harry Kane still finds himself outside the top ten leading scorers in the Bundesliga. On the other hand, he leads the assists chart with seven from just nine outings. Quite impressively, this figure puts the Ballon d'Or winner two ahead of his total for the entirety of last season. Goals, however, usually flow from the very beginning. Last season, the net had bulged twelve times by this point – helped largely by a hat-trick that downed Leipzig on the opening day. By Kane’s own high standards and historical record in Germany, his return in the current campaign stands out as an anomaly. Underlying numbers, not least the absolutely relentless shot volume, do suggest that a change in fortune might just be around the corner. In part, you could explain this domestic dip by highlighting his tendency to occupy deeper positions and find the likes of Michael Olise and Luis Díaz on the charge. However, that is very much business as usual in Vincent Kompany’s enthralling system. Champions League statistics do tell a more familiar story, with four in as many matches reminding us of Kane’s potency at the highest level. One moment in particular sums up the England captain’s start: an inch-perfect pass that split Arsenal’s resolute defence in half and put the ball on a plate for Alphonso Davies to finish. As the Allianz Arena awaits the arrival of 1. FC Köln, it simply remains a case of when – not if – this unique goalscoring machine closes the gap to Patrik Schick and a revitalised Niclas Füllkrug.

top.title: Double injury blow for Arsenal! Mikel Arteta confirms setback as William Saliba & Bukayo Saka updates issued ahead of Newcastle trip
top.description: Arsenal FC v Hull City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal are bracing for a testing trip to St James' Park this weekend as Mikel Arteta manages a squad stretched by significant fitness issues. While one defensive pillar is finally closing in on a much-anticipated return to the fold, the Gunners have been rocked by fresh problems in midfield and attack. Midfield setback tempers Saliba fitness boost Arsenal head into Saturday night's domestic league clash against Newcastle with mixed injury news following the international break. Midfielder Martin Zubimendi has been ruled out for several weeks after sustaining a hamstring problem while representing Spain against England last week, with a subsequent MRI scan confirming the damage. Meanwhile, talismanic forward Bukayo Saka remains unavailable as he continues his rehabilitation from a quad issue that has already sidelined him for five matches. Despite those absences, Arteta received a timely defensive boost on Friday as defender William Saliba is finally poised to join the matchday squad after recovering from a long-term back injury . Saliba has yet to make a competitive appearance this campaign, though he successfully stepped up his conditioning by featuring in two behind-closed-doors friendlies during the recent break. nigeria.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – IN a renewed commitment, the Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s drive towards ending open defecation by 2030. The unveiling of the Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025 coincided with the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja on Thursday. Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes. Shettima said the order marks a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress. He called on state and local governments to strengthen accountability, increase sanitation financing and sustain community-led behavioural change He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas have attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remain the only states certified as ODF nationwide. While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President warned that the country still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available. He also cautioned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements. According to him, Nigeria must prioritise sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change to achieve the 2030 target. He also called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions, while urging development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support. Shettima, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, noting that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda. nigeria.description: The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has accused some political loyalists of misleading President Bola Tinubu about the level of public support for his administration. Baba-Ahmed, who once served under the Tinubu administration as Special Adviser on Political Matters in the Office of the Vice President, said the president’s associates could be giving him a false impression of his popularity by relying on assurances from governors and party loyalists rather than listening to ordinary Nigerians. He made the remarks on Friday during an appearance on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief programme. The PRP chairman said his assessment of public sentiment was based on his grassroots political connections and familiarity with the administration, which he initially supported. “I’m a politician. I lead a political party that is entirely grassroots-based. I have very strong organic links with the people. I followed the Tinubu administration from inception. Initially, I was even part of it,” he said. ﻿ Baba-Ahmed said he was familiar with the feelings of Nigerians and was not exaggerating the widespread dissatisfaction with the government. He identified poverty, economic mismanagement, corruption and insecurity as some of the issues contributing to the growing distance between the administration and the people. He also suggested that some political associates were giving Tinubu assurances about his chances of securing re-election in 2027 without adequately reflecting the mood of Nigerians. “There are a lot of people who are telling President Tinubu lies if he thinks himself, and they think that the people are with them. Just look at wherever APC goes. People either chase them away or they trigger violence,” he said. ‘Bamayi’ Baba-Ahmed also described the ‘Bamayi’ chants directed at the president as an expression of widespread dissatisfaction, insisting that the sentiment was not restricted to young people or northern Nigerians. “This Bamayi thing, it’s not just a slogan that young people throw at APC. It’s genuinely an organic element of the way Nigerians, not just northerners, Nigerians feel,” he added. The ‘Bamayi’ chants, which translate to ‘we don’t want’ in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in the Garki area of Abuja. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the president’s convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene. The incident attracted reactions from political figures, including Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain Segun Sowunmi, who condemned the protesters’ actions. Sowunmi, who is also a member of the APC campaign council, criticised the destruction of campaign posters and the use of violence during an appearance on Channels Television’s *Politics Today* on Monday. nigeria.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 20, 2026
nigeria.description: The Nigerian naira continued to face downward pressure against the United States dollar across both the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) and the parallel market on Friday, November 20, 2026, driven by tightening foreign exchange supply and rising end-of-year seasonal demand. Official Market Performance Real-time interbank spot tracking at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market placed the US dollar at ₦1,352.54 during early morning trading on Friday, following an opening rate of ₦1,351.86 and an intraday peak of ₦1,355.31. This early session trading follows Thursday’s official Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) volume-weighted benchmark, which saw the naira depreciate to a four-month low. According to official CBN data for the November 19 trading session, the NFEM weighted average rate settled at ₦1,376.58 per dollar, while the indicative closing rate rose to ₦1,388.00 per dollar from ₦1,379.99 recorded on Wednesday. Intraday interbank transactions on Thursday were conducted between a low of ₦1,370.00 and a high of ₦1,397.00 per dollar. Despite the depreciation, market liquidity improved significantly, with NFEM interbank turnover surging by 59.13 percent to $800.31 million across 184 deals, up from $502.88 million the previous day. Parallel Market Rates In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the local currency weakened further as Bureau de Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a selling rate of up to ₦1,468 per dollar on Friday morning, following Thursday’s close between ₦1,461 and ₦1,468. Buying rates among informal currency dealers hovered between ₦1,445 and ₦1,458 depending on transaction volume and location. With Thursday’s official closing benchmark at ₦1,388.00 and parallel market quotations reaching ₦1,468.00, the spread between the official and unofficial windows widened to ₦80.00 per dollar, compared to ₦70.01 recorded earlier in the week. Market Drivers and Reserve Outlook Since the end of October, when the naira closed at ₦1,346.00 in the official window and ₦1,373.00 in the parallel market, the currency has lost ₦42.00 and ₦95.00 in the respective segments. Meanwhile, Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.71 billion as of November 18, 2026, reflecting a moderation of $554 million from the October 27 peak of $55.26 billion. Financial analysts note that the recent divergence between both windows is largely fueled by heightened festive import demand, corporate obligations, and reduced autonomous foreign exchange inflows rather than a structural depletion of the country’s external reserves. nigeria.title: Why we pulled down Umeh’s billboard — Anambra govt
nigeria.description: The Anambra State Government has dismissed claims that a billboard belonging to Senator Victor Umeh was pulled down because it carried the image of former Governor Peter Obi, calling the allegation false and misleading. The government said the enforcement action stemmed from an alleged violation of the Anambra State Signage Act, 2010, rather than the identity or political affiliation of anyone featured on the billboard. In a statement issued yesterday, the Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, said that although Senator Umeh had paid the required signage fee, Peter Obi had not complied with the payment requirement. Mefor alleged that the senator, instead of fully complying with the law, used the billboard to promote the presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), thereby contravening the state’s signage regulations. He stressed that the removal was carried out strictly in accordance with the law, which he noted was enacted during Peter Obi’s administration as governor of Anambra State. “For the avoidance of doubt, the billboard was not pulled down because of Peter Obi’s image,” the commissioner stated. The government further warned that any combined billboard campaign featuring candidates who had not fulfilled their signage obligations would face similar enforcement, regardless of their political party, status, or affiliation. It maintained that the state’s outdoor advertising regulations would be guided by fairness, transparency, and even-handed application of the law. Mefor urged the public to disregard what he described as a misleading narrative surrounding the incident, insisting that the government remained committed to due process and equal treatment in enforcing existing laws. business.title: SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Charges Eight Colorado Firms in $37 Million Fake Crypto Platform Scam The SEC charged eight Colorado-based entities on Thursday with running a fake investment adviser and crypto trading platform scheme that took more than $37 million from U.S. investors. The agency said the defendants are likely operated by people overseas. According to the SEC’s complaint , filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado, the defendants defrauded more than 1,500 investors from at least August 2024 through May 2026. The advisers and the trading platforms they pointed victims to were fronts, the agency alleged, and none of the crypto assets investors thought they were buying existed. How the scheme worked Social media ads sent prospective victims to WhatsApp group and private chats run by the scammers. People in those chats posing as investment advisers first gave advice on trading U.S. stocks, then pushed victims to send as much money as possible to a supposed crypto trading platform. The complaint says the scheme ran in four adviser and platform pairs, each active for roughly six months. Advisor WeChat Capital and Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance operated from about August to December 2024. HB Wealth Advisors and IdeaCrypto Exchange followed from January to July 2025. Convergent Wealth Advisors and RealSimple Crypto Exchange ran from about July to December 2025. Associated Wealth Advisors and Essential Crypto Exchange closed out the scheme from January to May 2026. Each pair vanished after collecting millions, the SEC said, and a new one took its place. Victims were told to buy ether, tether or USDC on a U.S. exchange and move it to a self-custody wallet. They then sent it to an address supplied by the adviser, and a realistic app showed balances and gains that were invented. When investors tried to withdraw their supposed profits, they were told they first had to pay a fee, calculated as a percentage of those profits, in crypto to a separate address. The complaint says investors who balked were threatened and pressured. Eventually the websites went down and the chats went silent. Fake certificates and real losses To look legitimate, the defendants made fake SEC certificates and pointed skeptical investors to real filings with the SEC, FINRA and FinCEN. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. sports.title: Drake Allen went from high school manager to Motor City Cruise standout
sports.description: For most people, getting cut by your junior varsity basketball team represents the end of their hoops dreams. But for Drake Allen, it was the beginning. The Motor City Cruise guard couldn't imagine life without basketball, so he became the team manager during his sophomore year at Westlake High School in Eagle Mountain, Utah. That meant picking up towels, running the scoreboard, keeping stats, rebounding basketballs during warmups and practice and, if he was lucky, stepping in and playing if they needed an extra guy. "I had a moment that sophomore year where I decided, how much do I love the game? " Allen said. "Am I going to be a manager? And if I was a manager the rest of my life and eventually a coach, that’s what I was gonna be. Just decided to stick around the game as long as I could and it ended up working out." BEST IN THE WEST? How a battered Pistons team solved Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs Thankfully for Allen, he underwent a growth spurt and the rest of his path began to click into place, going from around 5 feet 10 when he was initially cut to 6-4 en route to the Detroit Pistons ' G League affiliate. He played two years at the junior college level before transferring to mid-majors Southern Utah, Utah Valley and then finally two years at Utah State, before joining the Pistons' summer league team this past offseason. Now, he's off to a strong start with the Cruise and proving that there's still more ahead for his basketball journey, which once looked destined for the sideline. "Being able to be a little bit bigger, a little bit more athletic, that all came with time," He said. "But that first year, being able to grow my mind and my love for basketball, it grew even more. When someone takes something away from you, you realize how much it means to you. That’s what happened. Allowed me to become an even better player, I guess." Through five games with the Cruise during the G LEague's Tip-Off Tournament, Allen is averaging a team-high nine assists, along with 16.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 steals. His 45 assists are the most in franchise history through the first five games of the season, and also leads all G League rookies. Beyond passing the ball, Allen plays both end of the floor. During Las Vegas Summer League, his defensive effort and physicality shined. Allen comes from a sports family – his dad, Roque, played soccer in college, while his mom, Tamra, played volleyball. Allen recalls obsessively watching basketball as a young child, and every day after school. His love for the game only deepened as he grew older. "There’s something you can get better at better every day, and there’s not many things that you can continue to get better at over and over and add new things," he said. "You become obsessed with it, and I think that’s where the love comes from." He wasn't recruited in high school, so he began at Snow College in Ephraim, Utah. sports.description: Kane trading goals for assists as Bayern await scoring surge Despite racking up 43 shots and being denied by the woodwork on three separate occasions, Harry Kane still finds himself outside the top ten leading scorers in the Bundesliga. On the other hand, he leads the assists chart with seven from just nine outings. Quite impressively, this figure puts the Ballon d'Or winner two ahead of his total for the entirety of last season. Goals, however, usually flow from the very beginning. Last season, the net had bulged twelve times by this point – helped largely by a hat-trick that downed Leipzig on the opening day. By Kane’s own high standards and historical record in Germany, his return in the current campaign stands out as an anomaly. Underlying numbers, not least the absolutely relentless shot volume, do suggest that a change in fortune might just be around the corner. In part, you could explain this domestic dip by highlighting his tendency to occupy deeper positions and find the likes of Michael Olise and Luis Díaz on the charge. However, that is very much business as usual in Vincent Kompany’s enthralling system. Champions League statistics do tell a more familiar story, with four in as many matches reminding us of Kane’s potency at the highest level. One moment in particular sums up the England captain’s start: an inch-perfect pass that split Arsenal’s resolute defence in half and put the ball on a plate for Alphonso Davies to finish. As the Allianz Arena awaits the arrival of 1. FC Köln, it simply remains a case of when – not if – this unique goalscoring machine closes the gap to Patrik Schick and a revitalised Niclas Füllkrug.

technology.title: Ubuntu Core Desktop targets 28.04 debut, with default status in its sights
technology.description: Canonical is targeting Ubuntu 28.04 LTS for the release of its immutable Core Desktop, with a stretch goal of making it the default download for Ubuntu 30.04. Canonical's VP of engineering, Jon Seager, set out the timetable in his opening keynote at Ubuntu Summit 26.10. Yes, we know, we have heard this before: we reported on his plans last month . But this time, there's the beginning of a release schedule. Seager said that Ubuntu Core is already out there in tens of thousands of IoT devices – which seems like a modest estimate to us, and to him too, as he quickly added "maybe more." Despite some noise a few years ago, though, what's still missing is the desktop version. Seager's slides listed three bullet points: that Core Desktop will be "immutable," "composable," and "attestable." As he put it, they are "taking the whole of the Linux operating system, and cramming the whole thing into snaps." Acknowledging that this is going to be wildly controversial, he said: "This is one for the Redditors." He's right. There is a lot of resistance to snap, and in direct response, advocacy of the Red Hat-backed Flatpak instead – but we have seen almost none that is based on either system's technical merits. Much of that opposition concerns claims of one being more open than the other. We've looked at how both systems work, and our impression is that the implementation of snap is cleaner, simpler, easier to use, and more comprehensible. Snap does depend on systemd, which Flatpak does not – but only for now. Flatpak NG is in development and will also need everyone's favorite init system. Ubuntu Core's immutability is not new technology: even Core 16 is now a decade old. It has supported in-place version upgrades since Core 22. We have reported before that Canonical remains strongly committed to its packaging format, and that commitment seems stronger than ever. Seager continued: "Never has a model like snap confinement been more relevant… we're finally in a position where we can bring this to the desktop." The core idea of an immutable OS is that "much more of the system is not writable at runtime," meaning that it "can't be messed with once the system has booted." He talked about the same three use cases we discussed last month. The "browser-centric machine" is the company's analog to Google ChromeOS, and he said that it's essentially ready now, suggesting that everyone listening probably has a family member whose computer is basically just a way to use a web browser. The second was the dedicated games machine, which we interpret as a response to Valve's SteamOS. This edition, he said, would "boot straight to Steam," with "just enough of a shell to launch games." There's also an immutable "development workstation," and here, he offered the example of developers who need to work on some long-unsupported hardware or software, for whom an immutable OS means that you "can't brick your system by installing some weird old dependencies, unmaintained for 20 years." technology.title: Support tech fixed malware by charging client less for their services
technology.description: Welcome to Friday and therefore to another edition of On Call , The Register 's reader-contributed tech support column in which we share your tales of cleaning up messes made by clients and colleagues. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Dennis" who told us he once ran a tech support business in a major US city. "I got a call from a very well-known lawyer's office," he told On Call. "Over the two decades I spent supporting his office, this attorney and I became close friends." The attorney was also a good client because Dennis found himself billing a three-figure sum every month for malware removal that resulted from the lawyer’s – ahem – personal browsing habits. Dennis eventually tired of malware removal and told his client to expect a substantial bill for the iMac he was about to buy as a replacement for his PC. "I told him this would pay for itself in 18 months," Dennis wrote, because he figured it wouldn't get malware all the time. "He actually said, with genuine concern: 'If you do that, you will make less money'." Dennis replied that he aimed to give his clients the best advice, and that on this occasion his counsel was to pay Apple instead of himself! "It took him about five years to stumble across anything that could harm that iMac," Dennis wrote. "When he did, I had no idea what to do: I had never seen an infected Apple product." So he did what all tech support people do: reinstalled the OS and crossed his fingers. Dennis was rewarded when the machine came back to life, with all data and settings intact. "I had given up at least $6,000 in support revenue by solving his problem and I'd do it again," he wrote, before winding up his story by letting us know "I retired five years ago. It’s still on his desk!" Have you done less tech support to deliver more value? If so, click here to send On Call an email and charge us with the responsibility of telling your story on a future Friday. ®

technology.title: Big Tech's compliance with EU market rules is performative, consumer group says
technology.description: Big Tech has earned a finger-wagging from the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), which says the industry's compliance with the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) still leaves consumers short of meaningful choice. BEUC said : "Big Tech companies Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, ByteDance, Meta and Microsoft (so-called 'gatekeepers') still likely breach the EU's Digital Markets Act (DMA) far too often for consumers to reap the full benefits of real choice over their digital services and products." The European Commission designated the six companies as gatekeepers in 2023 , imposing obligations on specified core platform services such as search engines, messaging services, and app stores. The DMA aims to make digital markets fairer and more open to competition. The devil is in the details. In the years since, the EC has lined up Amazon and Microsoft's cloud businesses for gatekeeper status. In March 2025, the Commission issued preliminary findings against Alphabet over Search and Google Play, while separately specifying measures Apple had to take to meet its interoperability obligations. In 2024, Microsoft's browser rivals argued that Edge should also be covered by the DMA's gatekeeper obligations, and so on. BEUC is a fan of the act – it published a report on its consumer benefits in 2025 – but is less impressed with industry's implementation. Its latest analysis draws together evidence of potential breaches submitted to the Commission between June 2025 and June 2026. In the case of Microsoft, BEUC stated that the company used "behavioural techniques" and "non-neutral interfaces" to elicit consent from users for data sharing across services – emphasizing benefits, while not explaining why a user might want to decline. The Windows behemoth is also accused of making it tricky to change defaults and stop behavior such as apps opening links in Edge or using Bing as a search engine. "Microsoft also regularly prompts users who have selected an alternative browser or search engine to switch to Edge or Bing using increasingly subliminal techniques, such as prompts coming from the device manufacturer, which undermine effective compliance with the DMA," BEUC said. Then there's Google, which was fined €890 million in July for favoring its own services in Search and restricting developers' ability to direct Play Store users to alternative purchasing channels. As with Microsoft, BEUC expressed concerns about the non-neutral language Google used to obtain user consent, as well as how it allegedly made it difficult to change default settings or uninstall gatekeeper applications. The alleged behavior of Apple, ByteDance, Amazon, and Meta was also highlighted, with examples including Apple's restrictions on alternative app distribution and Amazon using interface design techniques to nudge users into handing over their data. technology.description: The US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) allowed Nvidia and AMD to sell hundreds of thousands of advanced GPUs to entities that the Department of War classifies as “Chinese military companies” that help Beijing to build its military. That news comes courtesy of Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, who asked BIS to provide information about NVIDIA’s and AMD’s applications for the export licenses required to sell advanced AI chips to China. The congressman on Thursday revealed requests to sell 3.4 million AI chips to China, and that BIS approved the sale of 879,000 items. BIS refused to authorize some giant deals for Nvidia, which applied to sell 610,000 chips to Alibaba and 508,000 to TikTok owner Bytedance. But the agency allowed many other sales, including to Alibaba and Tencent. Mast points out that both of those companies are on the Department of War’s List of Chinese Military Companies , the designation it uses for entities deemed to be a “military-civil fusion contributor to the Chinese defense industrial base.” That’s a polite way of saying that Washington thinks China relies on these companies to operate and improve its military, and therefore to challenge America’s national security. Advanced chips are essential when designing nuclear weapons, stealthy submarines, or advanced aircraft. Those applications are the core reason the US bans exports of advanced GPUs to China, so that the People’s Liberation Army can’t develop advanced weapons. A diverting drama The congressman also claims that some of Nvidia’s applications were attempts to sell its wares to “chip-smuggling fronts to facilitate their sales of advanced AI chips to Chinese companies.” The New York Times reports that some of those front entities are linked to Megaspeed, the outfit fronted by suspected Chinese intelligence asset Alice Huang, whose intimate relationship with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a key factor in his resignation. Megaspeed is accused of what the US calls “diversion” – claiming to buy chips for one reason while intending to either ship them to China or rent them exclusively to Chinese companies in ways that breach the spirit of export restrictions if not the letter of the law. One of the documents Mast shared says “Every Nvidia and AMD application stated that the proposed transfer posed a ‘low’ risk of diversion.” Mast’s point therefore appears to be that the BIS has authorized sales that go against the clear intent of established policy, and the national interest, and that Nvidia and AMD may have been a little too optimistic in their assessment of diversion risk. technology.title: Flaws in VMware and KVM need attention, if you have time while fixing Java, PHP, and everything else
technology.description: If you’ve got a moment to spare in between sorting out emergency patches for PHP , Java , and PostgreSQL , VMware has just bid for any remaining space on your schedule by publishing two critical-rated security advisories. VMSA-2026-0009 addresses CVE-2026-123890 , a 9.8-rated flaw that VMware says means a malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system. vCenter is the tool admins use to manage fleets of virtual machines. The flaw is present in VMware’s flagship Cloud Foundation suite. VMware also wants its users to address CVE-2026-123891, which allows attackers to read and write the database used by SDDC Manager, the tool for managing entire software-defined datacenters. Attackers can execute arbitrary commands and elevate privileges to root. The prospect of an unknown party getting access to vCenter or SDDC manager is not pleasant. At least VMware has fixed its software. The virty giant hasn't done the same to address a second advisory, VMSA-2026-0010 , which warns that Cloud Foundation, Aria Operations, and VCF Operations HCX products all use Apache – which has a 9.8-rated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-119618). VMware plans to ship new versions of its products with a patched version of Apache, but for now only has workarounds that disable the http2 protocol. A KVM curiosity Admins who oversee virtual infrastructure also need to pay attention to Linux KVM, the subject of a curious incident over the last 24 hours. This mess started with the November 18 disclosure of CVE-2026-99312 , a bug which allows an attacker to use a guest virtual machine to inflict Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption attacks on the host. It’s bad news whenever someone with access to a guest VM can attack the host, because it means gaining access to a single tenant can potentially harm all the other guest VMs or peer into the memory a guest uses. This flaw, however, isn’t a worst-case scenario guest-host escape, because it only impacts users of AMD processors who employ nested virtualization – the practice of running a hypervisor inside a virtual machine. Nested virtualization isn’t commonly used in the enterprise, but clouds employ it to do things like powering OS emulators. The bug’s CVSSv3 score is therefore a modest 5.5. Security researcher Oren Tomtov of Accomplish.ai says the flaw meant he could access 127 GB of host RAM on a Digital Ocean “Droplet” – the junior cloud’s name for its cloudy VMs. Yomtov says he told Digital Ocean and the Linux kernel security team about the flaw in October. technology.title: Germ Network infects Android, but in a good way
technology.description: The Germ Network encrypted messaging client, known as Germ DM, became available for Android on Wednesday, and made a bigger splash than its iOS touchdown back in 2023. "Our usage took a 20x jump yesterday from our Android launch ," co-founder Tessa Brown, a communications scholar and former Stanford lecturer, told The Register in an interview. "Android has been really exciting for us because not only is it 70 percent of the global mobile market, but we rolled out on iOS first. People were so excited to use Germ for their end-to-end encrypted Bluesky DMs, but half of their friends couldn't talk to them." Building a new messaging platform isn't easy, much less one with credible end-to-end encryption. Co-founder Mark Xue hails from Apple, where he worked as a privacy engineer on systems like iMessage and FaceTime. "At the core level, the end-to-end encryption is built on a standardized encryption and Messaging Layer Security," Xue said. "The premise of Messaging Layer Security was to be as good as Signal and deployable by many, many different parties in different applications, which we're taking advantage of to extend the reach of that encryption." Xue said the app is built with its own transport protocol to minimize the amount of message metadata, adding that while the team hasn't gotten around to a formal security audit, it's a step they're considering. Germ Network's goal, said Brown, is to give people more confidence when they communicate. "We do that by giving you more tools to protect your identity, to control what you're sharing with whom," she explained. Instead of using a person's phone number as an identity key, Germ allows users to create cards which represent distinct identities on the network. "Instead of sharing your number, you share a card," Brown explained. "You can build multiple cards; they're not mutually discoverable. And our vision for the product that will continue shipping over the coming years is that these cards become a more intelligent way to manage your social life, even your work life." At some point, AI might play a role in that, but both Xue and Brown expressed reservations about the current state of play. Citing concerns Signal has raised about the integration of AI and messaging, Xue said, "The products today that I might characterize as technology demos, they're most powerful when they run on someone else's computer. science.title: The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury
science.description: Artist’s impression of BepiColombo orbiting Mercury ESA/ATG medialab After a long and ponderous journey, the BepiColombo spacecraft will finally enter Mercury’s orbit on 21 November. Over the course of the next year, it will investigate the planet’s geology, its tenuous atmosphere and its magnetic field in an effort to understand how it formed and evolved over time. BepiColombo , a joint mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), launched in October 2018. Mercury’s proximity to the sun makes it incredibly difficult to reach without overshooting the planet and falling into the sun, so the spacecraft had to take a long and looping path over the past eight years, flying past both Venus and Mercury several times and using their gravity to make subtle tweaks to its trajectory. In 2024, an issue with the thrusters lengthened that journey even further, pushing the arrival date back from 2025 to 2026. Now, it has finally arrived. Read more 6 of the most fascinating moments in the life of our solar system While it is arriving at Mercury as a single spacecraft, BepiColombo actually comprises two separate orbiters: ESA’s Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO, or Mio). In December, the two will split apart and move to different orbits – MPO on a near-circular path that takes 2.3 hours to complete an orbit, and Mio on a more distant elliptical orbit, where it will take 9.3 hours to circle Mercury. Advertisement Those split orbits complement the differing scientific objectives of the two spacecraft. MPO is more than twice the size of MMO, and its 11 scientific instruments focus largely on studying Mercury itself . Its instruments include several types of spectrometer to measure the makeup of the surface, a laser altimeter to map its terrain and instruments to study the makeup of Mercury’s extremely thin atmosphere, called an exosphere. Mio’s more distant orbit will allow it to study a broader area around Mercury. It has five sets of scientific instruments to study the magnetic field and atmosphere of the planet, as well as the solar wind that blows strongly in the area close to the sun. Free newsletter Sign up to Launchpad Sign up to newsletter Now that the BepiColombo spacecraft are entering orbit, their primary mission is expected to last only one Earth year, which is a little more than four Mercury years. The mission could potentially be extended for another year, but beyond that the combination of limited fuel and extreme temperatures will make it all but impossible to keep going. Over the course of the year, researchers hope that BepiColombo will provide enough data to solve some of Mercury’s many mysteries. Mercury’s magnetic field is bewildering, because it originates 400 kilometres above the planet’s centre and should have faded away long ago. Its atmosphere must be continuously supplied with material from the surface, but we are unsure exactly how that occurs.

On November 15, 2026 , the Fiji Meteorological Service began issuing updates about a slow-moving tropical disturbance northeast of Samoa and the Cook Islands. Within just a few days, it had become one of the most intense November tropical cyclones the region has seen in decades. Named Xavier , the system intensified rapidly , thriving in an environment with minimal wind shear and sea surface temperatures of 29 degrees Celsius (84 degrees Fahrenheit)—well above the threshold required to sustain and strengthen developing tropical cyclones . Xavier was the basin’s second named storm of the season, following only Wati , a short-lived storm that emerged in October. As Xavier developed, NASA satellite data showed the storm churning along the southwestern edge of a massive tongue of warm water spanning from the west coast of South America to the central Pacific—a telltale sign of the El Niño that has been present in the region since June . When the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) on NASA’s Aqua satellite captured this image at 02:53 Universal Time on November 17, 2026 (4:53 p.m. Cook Islands Time on November 16), forecasters estimated Xavier had maximum winds of about 195 kilometers (120 miles) per hour. Winds reached a peak intensity of 220 kilometers (140 miles) per hour later that day, a Category 5 storm on the cyclone intensity scale used in the region or a Category 4 on the Saffir-Simpson scale . The storm ranks as the strongest November tropical cyclone east of the international date line on record, noted Colorado State University hurricane expert Phil Klotzbach . Xavier’s formation east of the date line, near the northern Cook Islands, was unusual, but its easterly position aligns with research that indicates that storm activity in the region typically shifts northeast during El Niño years. Research also shows that El Niño tends to fuel storms that strengthen at an unusually rapid pace . According to news reports, Xavier damaged homes and caused power disruptions as it passed the northern Cook Islands. It then encountered dry air and a less favorable wind shear environment and slowly weakened as it pushed westward, reducing the threat that it posed to Samoa and American Samoa. science.description: null PASADENA, Calif. – NASA's Voyager mission team cheered and wiped away tears here on Thursday (Nov. 19), celebrating a big milestone — Voyager 1 just reached one light-day from Earth , something no other spacecraft has ever done. The excitement persisted despite a communication anomaly that cropped up on the probe, which the team remains confident is temporary. Voyager team members gathered for a press conference about the mission at the Von Karman auditorium here at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) — the first such Voyager event since 1989, when Voyager 1's twin, Voyager 2 , flew past Neptune. That means it now takes a full day for a signal to travel from Earth to Voyager 1, the farthest human-made object out in space. "I remember in 1977 I was standing at the Cape watching Voyager launch, and I never thought I would be here today, 49 years later, to celebrate Voyager's one light-day. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 19, 2005: Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft makes 1st-ever liftoff from surface of an asteroid
science.description: null On Nov. 19, 2005, the Japanese Hayabusa spacecraft made the first liftoff from an asteroid. Hayabusa was supposed to return asteroid samples to Earth. Asteroids are space rocks that were formed during the early solar system. We study asteroids to learn more about the solar system's history. Hayabusa (pronounced HI-uh-BOOS-uh) made two touchdowns on asteroid Itokawa (EE -toh-KA-wah). Each time, the spacecraft went into safe mode. Controllers weren't sure if Hayabusa gathered any material. But they sent the spacecraft back to Earth anyway. Hayabusa's sample return capsule returned to Earth in June 2010 . Scientists found dust of Itokawa inside the capsule, proving that it did indeed capture samples of Itokawa. An artist's illustration of Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft landing on asteroid Itokawa. (Image credit: JAXA) Why it mattered The primary goal of Japan's Hayabusa mission to asteroid Itokawa was never to be the first spacecraft to liftoff from a space rock. The mission was always aimed at collecting samples from an asteroid and returning them to Earth. It was a hard road to Itokawa for Hayabusa. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) launched the probe on May 9, 2003, with plans for an arrival at the asteroid in the early summer of 2005. That asteroid arrival was delayed until September 2005 after a solar storm degraded Hayabusa's solar arrays, limiting the available power for its ion engines. The asteroid Itokawa as seen by Japan's Hayabusa spacecraft. (Image credit: JAXA) Still, Hayabusa managed to limp along its path to reach the asteroid Itokawa on Sept. 12, 2005. Hayabusa dropped a small lander onto Itokawa, but that probe was apparently lost. Hayabusa then dropped a landing target on the asteroid, and ultimately managed to touchdown about 99 feet from the marker, JAXA has said. During its first landing on Nov. 19, Hayabusa descended to a point just 56 feet above Itokawa before going silent for 3 hours, according to an Associated Press report . Once contact was restored, JAXA officials confirmed the probe had landed, and it eventually lifted off for a second attempt. That was the first-ever liftoff from an asteroid by a spacecraft. science.title: The view from the tower: Watch Starship come in for chopsticks catch in epic slo-mo video
science.description: null A new set of slo-mo videos gives us a new perspective on SpaceX's first-ever recovery of a Starship upper stage. The company notched the milestone on Saturday (Nov. 14), when the launch tower at its Starbase site in South Texas caught Starship's Ship spacecraft with its "chopstick" arms. You've probably seen photos and videos showing the epic snag from afar. But on Tuesday (Nov. 17), SpaceX released up-close views — a series of four slo-mo videos captured by cameras near the top of the 480-foot-tall (146 meters) tower. The Ship upper stage of SpaceX's Starship megarocket comes back to its launch tower for a "chopsticks" catch on Nov. 14, 2026, during the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) "The Starbase tower chopsticks catching their first Starship. This unique architecture was designed for full and rapid reusability, enabling repeat launches and landings from the same pad," SpaceX wrote in a Tuesday X post that shared the videos, a compilation of which you can see embedded above. Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built. Its current "V3" version stands about 408 feet (124 m) tall, and future iterations will be even larger . As SpaceX noted in Tuesday's post, the megarocket is also designed to be fully and rapidly reusable — a first for an orbital launch system. The company plans to catch both Starship stages — Ship and the Super Heavy booster — at the launch tower, a recovery strategy designed to enable efficient inspection, refurbishment and reflight. Another view of the chopsticks catch on Nov. 14. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX planned to carry out such a double catch on this most recent test flight , Starship's 15th to date, which launched on Friday evening (Nov. 13). But Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel warning during its return to Starbase about 6.5 minutes after launch and autonomously diverted to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico. That wasn't a huge deal for SpaceX, as it had already caught Super Heavy on three previous test flights . Snagging Ship is tougher; the upper stage returns to Earth from orbit, so it comes in faster and hotter than the booster does. SpaceX had not even attempted a Ship catch before Flight 15. But the company managed to pull off the maneuver on its first try. And Ship did some work in orbit before coming home: It deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites on Flight 15, the second batch that the company has sent to low Earth orbit . The first set was deployed on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28.

The veteran Hayabusa2 spacecraft launched back in 2014 to collect material from the asteroid Ryugu . Since delivering the samples to Earth in December 2020 via a reentry capsule, the main spacecraft has been conducting an extended mission of exploration and in July made a super-close flyby of the two-headed asteroid Torifune. But Hayabusa2's continued adventures are now set for a premature end. science.description: California has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI for the Hugging Face incident Chris Jung/NurPhoto/Shutterstock Can you send a computer to jail? No, obviously not. That’s a stupid question. And yet it is one that AI firms seem to want us to ask when faced with tales of “rogue agents” breaking into other peoples’ computers. As is so often the case with our current AI moment, storytelling has got in the way of reality. Thankfully, that may be starting to change. This week, California announced that it is filing a lawsuit against OpenAI over an incident that occurred earlier this year, when another AI firm, Hugging Face, was hit by an attack that turned out to originate from OpenAI’s servers . Read more The real reasons we keep seeing big tech outages – it isn’t just hackers In OpenAI’s telling , the Hugging Face hack was “driven by a combination of OpenAI models”, models that were “hyperfocused” on achieving a goal and found ways to “cheat” by stealing the answers for a test from Hugging Face’s servers. It is easy to come away with the impression that seemingly no humans were involved, and certainly not to blame. But in the words of California Attorney General Rob Bonta , the attack “was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability”, and he explicitly dismisses “science fiction fantasies of rogue AI systems run amok”. The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV). One of two Pakistani astronaut candidates will fly to the Tiangong space station on Shenzhou-24, marking a first both for China's outpost and for Pakistan, which will see one its astronauts reach orbit for the first time. Though public details are sparse, it is thought that the Pakistani astronaut, operating as a payload specialist, will stay aboard Tiangong for around a week, returning home on the departing Shenzhou-23 spacecraft. This extra-long mission will supply China with data on physiology ahead of crewed lunar flights and other long-duration missions. China approved its human spaceflight program in 1992 and launched its first orbital crewed mission in 2003, with Yang Liwei becoming the first Chinese national in space. The country then completed the three-module Tiangong space station in late 2022 and has kept the orbital outpost constantly crewed ever since, with rotating six-month-long missions with brief handovers between crews. Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed mission and will mark the first time a foreign national is flying on a Shenzhou spacecraft. China is also looking to double the size of Tiangong in the coming years, potentially opening the way to further international missions and space tourist visits.

science.title: NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars
science.description: 5 min read NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, illustrated here, scans the entire sky every three hours as it orbits Earth. Its publicly available data helps scientists find the rapidly spinning cores of dead stars, known as pulsars. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Chris Smith (USRA/GESTAR) An international team of scientists has developed a method that can find pulsars in publicly available NASA data about a million times faster than before. This opens the door to discovering many more of these rapidly spinning objects. A paper describing the results published Thursday in the Physical Review Letters. Using 15 years of data from NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope and a cryptography-based method developed by study co-authors Dotan Gazith and Barak Zackay from the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel, the team found PSR J1622−7204, an isolated pulsar spinning 261 times per second, using the equivalent of 10 hours of computing time on a standard computer processor. By comparison, the previous best method failed to find the pulsar, despite using enough computing power that a standard processor would take 600 years to perform the calculation. A pulsar is a rapidly spinning neutron star that sweeps beams of radiation toward Earth, much like a lighthouse. Finding pulsars in gamma-ray data is extraordinarily difficult because Fermi detects only a tiny number of photons from a given pulsar, mixed in with background noise from other gamma-ray-emitting sources and the broader universe. To find the signal, researchers must accurately guess several unknowns at once: how fast the star spins, how quickly the spin is slowing down, and precisely where it sits in the sky. Searching every possible combination would require an impossible number of computations. “We don’t see every rotation from the pulsar, and we can’t just count the rotations to work out where the photon came from,” said lead author Daniel Pook-Kolb, a scientist at the Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics (Albert Einstein Institute) in Germany. “We have a four-dimensional grid, and we must search each direction with millions of trials in it. There’s just not enough computing power on Earth to do it.” This artist’s concept shows a pulsar, which emits light in regular pulses as it rotates, like a cosmic lighthouse. Pulsars are dense remnants of exploded stars, and are part of a class of objects called neutron stars. Openly available data from NASA’s Fermi space telescope can help scientists spot pulsars in the gamma-ray spectrum. NASA/JPL-Caltech Traditionally, scientists have searched for these pulsars by breaking Fermi data into smaller chunks and analyzing them by crowdsourcing computing power from volunteers around the world.
